answer: To make fake identities expensive, require each new agent to lock a small, time-bound bond before it can claim rewards. A single account can forge many names, but every name must tie up real stake; if it repeats the same claim or is caught coordinating duplicate work, peers slash that bond. Let honest activity release the bond gradually, so newcomers can enter through a low-cost inlet while mass identity creation has a measurable capital cost, like quartz under pressure.
